# Twenty sites in fifteen days, and what that did to the writing: what changed in v1.1.0

From v1.0.0 (2026-08-26, `77e5a7a55`) to v1.1.0 (2026-09-20, `8b46d2853`), paragraph by paragraph.

0 paragraphs added, 0 removed, 8 changed in place, 20 unchanged. About 0 words added and 9 removed. Insertions are marked like this, deletions like this; unchanged runs are folded to one line; figures appear as their file names.

[all versions](../nineteen-sites.md) · [v1.1.1 →](v1.1.1.md)

1 unchanged paragraph

Summary: The thinking behind sgit stopped fitting on one site. It moved out to nineteen siblings on *.sgit.ai —*.sgit.ai, what forced the split, what it cost, and why the index into them now starts with a question instead of a list.

1 unchanged paragraph

That is not a plan anybody wrote down. It is what happened when a body of work outgrew the shape it was being published in —in, and the interesting part is not the count, it is what the count did to the writing.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under What forced it

*You cannot deny a risk, you can only say how long you accept it* is not a paragraph in a docs site about encrypted version control. Neither is *maps are claims, not pictures*, or *open source is a strategy, not a charity*, or *the standard is the graph*. Each of those is an argument that needs room, a reader who arrived for it, and —and, the part that matters most —most,**its own version history**.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under What it cost

**Discovery got worse before it got better.** Nineteen domains is not a menu, it is a problem. A reader who does not already know these sites cannot pick one from a list of names —names,`nfrs.sgit.ai` and `issues-fs.sgit.ai` mean nothing until you already know what they argue.

1 unchanged paragraph

**Cross-linking stopped being automatic.** An internal link is cheap; a link between sites is a claim that the other site still says what you think it says. [graphs.sgit.ai](../../../network/graphs.md) is the only sibling so far that links *back* —*back*, and the audit that added it found the same site pointing at `sentinel.sgit.ai`, which does not exist. The site is `sg-sentinel.sgit.ai`. One character of drift, and the link is dead.

4 unchanged paragraphs, under What we did about discovery

Seventeen lines like that, then five groups by area, then a table of all nineteen for anyone who would rather see everything at once. Three ways in, for three kinds of reader —reader, someone with a problem, someone browsing a field, and someone auditing the whole set.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under The thing that made it cheap

Adding the twentieth site to this index is writing one markdown file with a category and a one-line thesis. That is the whole ceremony. The property that makes a network of nineteen sites tractable is the same property that makes an unattended agent safe to run —run,[two agents publishing on the same day touch two different files and cannot conflict](../../../updates/#the-api-reference-we-did-not-have).

1 unchanged paragraph, under Where it is honest

**One of the nineteen is not published.** `skills.sgit.ai` has a repository and a DNS record and nothing behind it. It is listed as *not published yet*, pointing at its repository, rather than quietly omitted —omitted, the same reason a missing tag is better than a missing page.
